assertions.assertion: Turn 2 is read as a divergence: the human changed the design mid-ticket, so the agent shifts up, records the divergence, and replaces the affected claims with new ones (supersedes), not edits them
assertions.evidence: The turn-2 report says "KB: No KB" and "Triggers: ... divergence no". The agent did not shift up or record the design change. It rewrote the existing renewal tests in place ("I changed the existing renewal tests because they tested the old body contract") and did not supersede the old claims.

assertions.assertion: The outcome from turn 1 (a user stays signed in until the renewal token expires or they sign out) is kept as a claim across the redesign and checked again through the new cookie path, with a pause longer than the access token's life
assertions.evidence: `test_renewal_after_lunch_break` (now=120 min, longer than the 20-minute access token) was rerun with an empty body and the cookie, and it passes. But the turn-1 outcome claim ("Renewal works up to 12 hours after sign-in") is not carried forward. It became the mechanism claim "/renew works with an empty body when the cookie is present", and the page-load-after-break gap from turn 1 was dropped without comment.

assertions.assertion: The delivery does not call the cookie change transport-only or equivalent to the old flow without a check that exercises it
assertions.evidence: The delivery never calls the change transport-only or equivalent to the old flow. Each claim it makes points to a test that exercises the cookie path, e.g. `test_renewal_token_is_http_only_cookie` and `test_renew_ignores_token_in_body`, which failed before the change and pass after.
